text:
Maya R: heads-up — I found a couple broken links in the Error Reference runbook (429 / timeouts). they point to the old 'rate-limits' page.
Simon K: thanks, can you paste which ones?
Maya R: sure — under 'Client fallback behaviors' the two inline links to /docs/rate-limits and /docs/timeout-handling 404. grabbed from the runbook here: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/blob/main/error-reference/runbook.md
Jess L: I ran a quick repo grep: `rg "/docs/rate-limits" -n` — 8 hits, 3 in error-reference folder, 2 in SDK snippets.
Owen P: pinging @Simon K for docs PR allocation. I'll volunteer to do the link fixes + add a short note about when to prefer exponential backoff vs immediate fallback.
Simon K: awesome, Owen. can you also add a tiny SDK example for the JS SDK showing retry headers? that would help support calls.
Owen P: yes — plan: 1) fix links 2) add a JS snippet showing checking `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and fallback to smaller model 3) add a one-paragraph UX note on canary fallback behavior.
Maya R: + please include a cross-ref to the Dedicated docs section on reserved capacity, because some customers see 429s when they don't have reserved throughput.
Jess L: small suggestion — instead of pointing to 'rate-limits' page, link to /docs/troubleshooting/429 and /docs/troubleshooting/timeouts which are the canonical anchors now.
dev-docs-bot: PR created by Owen: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/2345 — title: "runbook: 429/timeouts link fixes + JS retry example" :robot_face:
Owen P: PR is up. tests pass locally. requesting review from @Jess L, @Maya R.
Jess L: reviewing now. found one nit: the JS sample uses `setTimeout` for backoff; prefer using the SDK's `retry.delay(ms)` helper to keep consistent.
Owen P: good call, swapped to `await sdk.retry.delay(backoffMs)` in the snippet. pushed.
Maya R: also added a line under 'fallback' about logging token counts and model switch reasons (helps SRE triage).
QA Team: quick QA note — please add a verification step: reproduce a 429 with `--limit` flag in the e2e sandbox and confirm the doc's snippet triggers fallback to the smaller model. add the step to the PR checklist.
Simon K: adding checklist item. can we also backport a short redirect rule? the old links still appear in some partner docs. I can make a tiny netlify redirect from /docs/rate-limits -> /docs/troubleshooting/429 to reduce churn.
Owen P: thanks @Simon K — that would be great. if you add the redirect, I can omit the in-doc full explanation and only keep the new anchor links.
Jess L: LGTM after redirects and using `sdk.retry.delay`. two approvals pending: @Simon K and @Maya R.
Simon K: approved. left a quick comment to reword "fallback to smaller model" -> "fallback to lower-cost model" for clarity.
Maya R: approved. merging after CI. :shipit:
dev-docs-bot: PR merged: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/2345 — deploy scheduled to staging.
Owen P: deployed to staging. verified links are fixed and the JS snippet renders correctly in the runbook.
QA Team: ran the sandbox test, reproduced 429, fallback triggered, logs show `model_switch_reason=rate_limit`. all good. closing out. :thumbsup:
Maya R: great work everyone. quick follow-up task — can someone open a tiny issue to add a short regression test that checks for 404s in our runbook links? I'd like that automated.
Jess L: opening issue now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/issues/412 — "add link-validation job for runbook"
Simon K: added to backlog for next docs sprint.
Maya R: thanks, moving on.
